title: (No AI) Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/Siri-AI-Being-invoked-3.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

_Bloomberg's_ Mark Gurman says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to [accelerate the Siri roadmap](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2026-11-08/apple-explores-turning-siri-ai-into-chatgpt-dots-like-agent-ios-28-shake-up) and deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI's Dots or Meta's Muse. While Federighi has delivered a functional version of Siri AI on an incredibly short timeline, the company has no illusions that it's keeping pace with its rivals.

title: (No AI) Elvis and Eminem rights holders are suing Suno
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![Elvis Presley](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/22202367/517216004.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Suno is facing yet another [pair of lawsuits](https://variety.com/2026/music/news/elvis-eminem-sue-suno-ai-music-generator-1236941798/). A group of rights holders of Elvis Presley's music and the publisher of some of Eminem's biggest records are suing the AI music company, claiming it illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic those artists. The lawyers in the Presley suit claim that Suno has violated Tennessee's Ensuring Likeness Voice and Image Security (ELVIS) Act, which makes it illegal for an AI company to clone a singer's voice.

In the suit, lawyers representing Presley's rights holders argue that "Suno has mechanically encoded itself with artists' identities, hard-work, creativity, and time, and harnessed them all for …
